rv.q: The resulting double bill now arrives in the West End: a beautifully modulated and quietly devastating evening of school drama.
It's a whipsmart marvel of a production.

Nicholas Farrell's central performance as Crocker-Harris – the dry-as-a-Greek-textbook schoolteacher mocked by his pupils, taken for granted by his employer and held in contempt by his wife (a bitingly selfish Anna Chancellor, left) – is an understated masterclass.
Certainly, the two plays compliment each other, and together form what is undoubtably an enjoyable evening of theatre.

cn.t: This double bill of public school dramas earns strong reviews, with critics praising the thematic pairing and performances that explore conformity and emotional repression in British educational settings.
